deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Two coaxial plane plates (a condenser), A and B, of radius R, are a distance 2ε apart. Each plate carries a uniform part of the surface density (+P on one, -P on the other) plus an edge-singular part proportional to 1/sqrt(1-ρ²/R²). The field point P lies on the common axis, at distance x from the centre C of plate B and at distance x+2ε from the centre C' of plate A. V1 is the potential of the uniform parts:
V1 = 2πP[(√(R²+x²) - x) - (√(R²+(x+2ε)²) - (x+2ε))].
Each bracket is the classical axial potential of a uniformly charged disc, interpreted geometrically as DP - CP, where D is the rim point of the plate in a meridian plane.

Step 1 (trigonometric form). Put φ = ∠DPC and φ' = ∠D'PC. In the right triangle CPD we have tan φ = R/x, so DP = x sec φ. Likewise D'P = (x+2ε) sec φ' with tan φ' = R/(x+2ε). Hence
V1 = 2πP( x sec φ - x - (x+2ε) sec φ' + (x+2ε) ).
Riemann then writes this as 2πP( x(sec φ - sec φ') - 2ε sec φ + 2ε ). The correct regrouping is 2πP( x(sec φ - sec φ') - 2ε sec φ' + 2ε ); see the errors list.

Step 2 (practical remark). This form is convenient for numerical work. One looks up in a trigonometric table the secant belonging to tangent R/x (or cotangent x/R), which avoids extracting square roots. Since φ depends on x and R only implicitly, he wants V1 as an explicit function of x and R. He proposes the binomial series, expanding in x/R for x<R and in R/x for x>R.

Step 3 (expansion for x<R; my explicit form). With f(t) = √(R²+t²) - t = R + t²/(2R) - t⁴/(8R³) + t⁶/(16R⁵) - ... - t, we get V1/(2πP) = f(x) - f(x+2ε). Ordered in powers of x:
- x⁰ term: 2ε - (2ε)²/(2R) + (2ε)⁴/(8R³) - (2ε)⁶/(16R⁵) + ...
- x¹ term: -(x/R)(2ε - 4ε³/R² + 12ε⁵/R⁴ - ...)
- x² term: +(x²/R²)(3ε²/R - 15ε⁴/R³ + ...)

Factoring out 2ε gives
V1 = 4πPε[ 1 - ε/R + ε³/R³ - 2ε⁵/R⁵ ... - (x/R)(1 - 2ε²/R² + 6ε⁴/R⁴ ...) + (x²/R²)(3ε/(2R) - 15ε³/(2R³) ...) ... ].

Riemann's version of this expansion has the same structure (constant, x/R and x²/R² groups) but wrong coefficients. He writes the constant group as 2ε - ½(2ε)²/R + ¼(2ε)⁴/R³ - ⅜(2ε)⁶/R⁵, giving 4επP[1 - ε/R + 2ε³/R³ ...]. He writes the linear group as -(x/R){ε - 2ε³/R² + (9/4)ε⁵/R⁴}, and after factoring as -(x/(2R)){1 - 4ε²/R² + (9/2)ε⁵/R⁴}. He writes the quadratic group as +(x²/R²){3ε²/R² - ...}.

Purpose. This is part of the calculation of the axial potential of a two-plate condenser. V2, the part from the edge-singular charge, is treated on the next page and gives 2πP1·R(arctan(R/x) + arctan(R/(x+2ε))).
errors: Regrouping slip in the trigonometric form. -(x+2ε)sec φ' + (x+2ε) gives -x sec φ' - 2ε sec φ' + 2ε, so the term should be -2ε sec φ', not -2ε sec φ. The slip is carried into the total potential on the next page.

Binomial coefficients in the constant (x⁰) group are wrong. The correct series is 2ε - (2ε)²/(2R) + (2ε)⁴/(8R³) - (2ε)⁶/(16R⁵), i.e. coefficients 1/2, 1/8, 1/16, not 1/2, 1/4, 3/8. Consequently the factored bracket should read 1 - ε/R + ε³/R³ - 2ε⁵/R⁵, not 1 - ε/R + 2ε³/R³.
Linear-in-x group is wrong. The correct form is -(x/R)(2ε - 4ε³/R² + 12ε⁵/R⁴), not -(x/R)(ε - 2ε³/R² + (9/4)ε⁵/R⁴). After factoring 2ε it should be -(x/R)(1 - 2ε²/R² + 6ε⁴/R⁴).

Riemann's two linear-group lines are mutually inconsistent. Dividing his own first line by 2ε gives -(x/(2R))(1 - 2ε²/R² + (9/8)ε⁴/R⁴), not his 1 - 4ε²/R² + (9/2)ε⁵/R⁴. The exponent ε⁵/R⁴ in the factored line is also dimensionally inconsistent.

Quadratic group: the correct term is (x²/R²)(3ε²/R - ...) before factoring, and (x²/R²)(3ε/(2R) - 15ε³/(2R³)) after factoring 4πPε. Riemann's 3ε²/R² inside the factored bracket omits the division by 2ε and one power of 1/R.
Convergence: the joint series in x/R requires x+2ε<R, not merely x<R; this is not stated.
(Next page, for context.) The large-x expansion with leading constant 2ε cannot be right, since V1 → 0 as x → ∞; the correct leading term is 2πP·R²ε/x². This error is not on the present page.

results.what: Axial potential of a uniformly charged disc written as 2πP(DP - CP) = 2πP·x(sec φ - 1), with tan φ = R/x, for table-based computation
results.modern_name: on-axis potential of a uniformly charged disc
results.usually_credited_to: classical potential theory (Laplace/Poisson era); textbook standard

results.what: Binomial-series expansion of the condenser's uniform-part potential in powers of x/R (and of R/x for x>R)
results.modern_name: multipole/Taylor expansion of the axial disc potential

results.what: Context: potential of a circular-plate condenser with uniform plus 1/sqrt(R²-r²) edge density
results.modern_name: Kirchhoff/Maxwell circular-plate condenser problem; Green–Cavendish charged-disc density

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine potential-theory computation: the axial disc potential, its trigonometric rewriting, and binomial expansion, with several arithmetic slips. Only the general context (an early approximate treatment of the plate condenser, anticipating Kirchhoff 1877) is of mild historical interest, and that belongs to the surrounding pages rather than this one.

checkable.asserts: DP = x*sec(phi) when tan(phi)=R/x (should simplify to 0)
x^0 group = 2e - 2e^2/R + 2e^4/R^3 - 4e^6/R^5 + ..., i.e. coefficients 1/2,1/8,1/16 on powers of 2e
for large x, V1/(2πP) ~ R^2*e*u^2 (u=1/x), no constant term, contradicting the next page

transcription_corrections: First expansion line: the leading coefficient appears written over an earlier sign/number ('±½'); the reading −½ is fine.
In the linear group the crossed-out item is a fraction ε/(…) written over; the surviving reading 'ε − 2ε³/R² + (9/4)ε⁵/R⁴' is as on the image.
In the last line the crossed-out mark is before R² in the denominator, i.e. x²/R² with a struck-out character; the bracket reads {3ε²/R² − …} (the exponent of R is overwritten).
The density symbol written as 'P' looks like a script ρ/P on the image; it is the same constant P as on the previous page.
